subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should native `openclaw backup create` grow user-controlled ignore-pattern flags now, and if so should the accepted design be the linked PR's smart defaults/protected-path contract or a narrower exclude-only surface?
rationale: The issue is a feature request for new CLI behavior on a security-sensitive backup path; the choice affects restorability, sensitive file handling, JSON output compatibility, and whether ClawHub backup plugins are considered sufficient for some workflows.

options.title: Review the linked native implementation
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the candidate fix and require maintainer approval on defaults, protected paths, compatibility, and real backup proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the native surface
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that only adds explicit `--exclude`/`--exclude-file` without smart defaults or auto-detected ignore files.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub backup plugins
options.body: Close the native feature direction only if maintainers decide focused external backup plugins such as Keep My Claw are the preferred path and built-in pattern controls should not be added.

recommendation.title: Review the linked native implementation
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the candidate fix and require maintainer approval on defaults, protected paths, compatibility, and real backup proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the backup CLI surface introduced in `0ecfd37b44656f3b1ef08268e3b5c6d975107a26`.
